title: Brent Crude Is Up 85% Since January. OXY, XOM, and CVX Are Playing It Very Differently. - AOL.com
content: Oil prices have risen dramatically in 2026, driven higher by the geopolitical conflict in the Middle East. Some of the most important oil companies didn't benefit as much as you would expect because of regional exposure, timing, and hedging activity. 10 stocks we like better than Occidental Petroleum › Occidental Petroleum (NYSE: OXY) beat Wall Street estimates by a wide margin when it reported first-quarter 2026 earnings. Analysts were expecting earnings of $0.59 per share, but the company reported $1.06 per share. That's an impressive beat, but management admits that it could have done better. What's going on with the company and with peers like Chevron (NYSE: CVX) and ExxonMobil (NYSE: XOM)? One of the first big problems in the quarter for oil companies was the timing of the oil price spike. Most of the advance occurred after the geopolitical conflict in the Middle East began, so the spike that has pushed oil prices up 85% in 2026 as of this writing didn't really get underway until March. So, energy companies only benefited from higher oil prices for a short period. Will AI create the world's first trillionaire? For example, Wall Street is projecting Oxy to earn $1.58 per share in the second quarter. But another issue hampered Oxy's performance in the first quarter: hedging. Oil companies routinely hedge their production to protect against price movements in energy markets. In this case, that hedging turned into a headwind. Oxy, which is much less exposed to the Middle East than Exxon or Chevron, was a relative standout. At the other extreme was Exxon, which has more exposure to the region and saw its production impacted. That said, its $1.16 per share in earnings beat the analyst call of $1.01. But hedging led to a $700 million earnings hit. That should be reversed in the second quarter as shipments hedged are delivered. Still, the short-term impact is worth noting as you examine the business. Chevron, meanwhile, fell between Exxon and Oxy, with its $1.41 per share earnings beating Wall Street's $0.97 per share call. But once again, the company's hedging activity was a headwind, as management took a $2.9 billion charge related to it. Hedging is company-specific, with each company adopting a different approach. And because hedging is a proprietary activity, investors won't know about the impact, good or bad, until the company releases quarterly results. That said, the refining operations of Exxon and Chevron performed weakly, with timing and hedging both playing a role. Oxy recently sold its downstream business at the start of 2026, so this business wasn't a meaningful issue for the company in the quarter. Simply put, there are a lot of moving parts to consider when you look at individual energy companies. In the end, Oxy, Exxon, and Chevron are all benefiting from rising energy prices, but the way they are playing the rise is slightly different. And that, in turn, is leading to different outcomes. The dividend yield on the S&P 500 is a mere 1.1%, rounded up, but that doesn't mean the entire equity market lacks attractive equity-income opportunities. It's simply a matter of knowing where to look. Interestingly, some of the smallest sectors in the S&P 500 are where some of the largest dividend yields are found. All right, so 2.7% might not qualify as "jaw-dropping," but investors shouldn't be dismayed because the energy sector is home to an array of dividend payers (and growers) with higher yields with the potential to reward long-term investors. In fact, there are 69 U.S.-listed energy stocks carrying dividend yields of at least 3% and sporting gains over the past 12 months. Here's an interesting trio to consider. One of the blue chip dividend stocks in the oil patch, Chevron (NYSE: CVX), yields 3.7%, but more important than that above-average yield is the integrated oil giant's dividend reliability. The payout increase unveiled by the company earlier in 2026 marks the 39th consecutive year in which Chevron has boosted its dividend, providing income investors with the like-clockwork dependability they so desire. Above-average yields and long track records of dividend growth are nice, but investors are right to demand dividend safety, too. Chevron offers that because it has operational expertise exceeding that of some rivals and has proven to be an adept cost-cutter over the years. Obviously, cost containment is vital in the capital-intensive exploration and production sector because it lowers producers' break-even points. Said differently, adept cost managers like Chevron can continue generating and growing profits even if oil prices slide. Speaking of oil prices, thanks to its cost-cutting prowess and a portfolio chock-full of high-quality assets, Chevron can, by some estimates, fund its dividend at $40 per barrel. That's $57 below where West Texas Intermediate (WTI) settled on May 22. Adding to the safety net is management's commitment to shareholder rewards, which totaled $6 billion in the first quarter, spread across buybacks and dividends. With a market capitalization of $2.7 billion, Delek Logistics Partners (NYSE: DKL) is a mid-cap stock, which might explain some of its anonymity. But with a dividend yield of 8.8% and fresh off an April payout increase, this stock arguably deserves more attention in the energy dividend conversation. This midstream operator has multiple catalysts for share price appreciation and potential dividend growth, including year-over-year earnings growth of 23.7%. Additionally, the company is shedding its "captive" status from Delek (NYSE: DK), which owns 63.3% of the logistics firm, as it expects to source 80% of its 2026 earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) from third parties. Experienced equity income investors know that midstream energy is a great place to find dividends, but on the surface, it's hard to tell many of these operators apart. Delek Logistics breaks from the pack by combining crude, natural gas, and water services, giving it some wide-moat advantages. This energy stock may also be appealing to value investors because management views it as the cheapest company in the space, with a compelling growth trajectory ahead. Kinetik Holdings (NYSE: KNTK) is another mid-cap midstream operator that doesn't generate a lot of buzz, but it may also be a friend to dividend investors. It yields 6.3% and boosted its payout in January. Kinetik, which has a significant footprint in the Delaware Basin, recently reiterated its 2026 EBITDA guidance with CEO Jamie Welch noting the company has "meaningful insulation" from near-term oil price gyrations. Welch also noted customers are pulling forward activity to 2027, positioning Kinetik for what could be another solid year. There's even more to like with this midstream operator. Kinetik is buying back stock and reducing debt, and those perks are accruing as the stock trades at discounts to peers despite Kinetik generating better net margins. content: Eni S.p.A. E and its partners, PETROCI and Vitol, approved the final investment decision (FID) for the Baleine Phase 3 project during a ceremony in Abidjan. The decision marks a major milestone for the Baleine field, the largest hydrocarbon discovery ever made in Cote d’Ivoire and highlights the country’s growing importance as an energy hub in West Africa. The Phase 3 expansion aims to significantly increase production from 60 thousand barrels per day (MBPD) to 150 MBPD, while gas output is expected to reach 200 million cubic feet per day (MMcf/d) from 80 MMcf/d. The project includes the construction of a new floating production, storage and offloading (FPSO) unit designed to improve operational efficiency, safety and environmental performance. By continuing its phased and fast-track development model, Eni is expected to reach early production milestones and reduce costs by leveraging existing infrastructure. The integrated energy giant emphasized that all gas produced from the project will be supplied to Cote d’Ivoire’s domestic market to support electricity generation, industrial development and national energy security. Since entering Cote d’Ivoire in 2015, Eni has made significant discoveries, including Baleine and Calao, strengthening offshore exploration activity in the country. Beyond energy development, E continues to support local communities through investments in education, healthcare, training and local business development initiatives. However, it's crucial to note that they remain very much invested in the stock and that sale only reduced their holding by 4.4%. In fact, the recent sale by Director John Hess was not their only sale of Chevron shares this year.  They previously made an even bigger sale of -US$83m worth of shares at a price of US$152 per share.     That means that even when the share price was below the current price of US$191, an insider wanted to cash in some shares.  When an insider sells below the current price, it suggests that they considered that lower price to be fair. That makes us wonder what they think of the (higher) recent valuation. title: Chevron Begins Drilling New Well at Egypt's Narges Gas Field - The Globe and Mail
content: Chevron CorporationCVX has launched a new drilling operation in Egypt’s Mediterranean-based Narges natural gas field, marking a significant milestone in its long-term expansion strategy across the Eastern Mediterranean energy sector. The drilling campaign highlights the growing importance of Egypt as a regional natural gas powerhouse while reinforcing Chevron’s ambition to substantially increase production capacity in one of the world’s most strategically valuable energy regions. The drilling operation commenced aboard the advanced drillship “Stena Forth,” which recently arrived in Egyptian waters to begin exploration and development work at the offshore concession. The Narges field is operated by CVX in partnership with Italy’s Eni S.p.A.E, the UAE’s Mubadala Energy and Egypt’s Tharwa Petroleum Company. The collaboration demonstrates the increasing confidence international energy giants have in Egypt’s offshore natural gas reserves and the country’s expanding role within global energy markets. Egyptian minister of Petroleum and Mineral Resources Karim Badawi personally inspected the launch of operations, emphasizing the government’s commitment to accelerating production from undeveloped offshore gas discoveries. The Egyptian government considers projects such as Narges essential for increasing domestic energy security, reducing reliance on imports and strengthening the country’s broader economic position amid rising energy demand. Egypt has intensified efforts to maximize domestic natural gas production as part of a broader national strategy designed to stabilize local energy supplies and minimize the financial burden associated with importing fuel. The development of the Narges field represents a major component of this strategy, particularly as Egypt seeks to balance growing domestic consumption with its ambitions to remain a leading regional energy exporter. Badawi praised CVX and its partners for maintaining close coordination with the Egyptian petroleum sector and the Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Company to overcome operational challenges and accelerate offshore drilling plans. Egyptian authorities are increasingly focused on bringing undeveloped discoveries into production as quickly as possible, particularly in the Mediterranean basin, where several promising gas reserves have been identified in recent years. The Narges field is viewed as a strategically important asset capable of enhancing Egypt’s natural gas supply network while supporting industrial growth, electricity generation and long-term energy stability. Expanding local production remains a top priority for the Egyptian government as it seeks to reduce exposure to global energy market volatility and rising import costs. The launch of drilling activities at the Narges field further elevates the importance of the Eastern Mediterranean as one of the world’s fastest-growing natural gas exploration regions. Over the past decade, massive offshore discoveries across the Mediterranean have transformed the regional energy landscape and attracted substantial investments from international oil and gas companies. Egypt has emerged as a dominant player within this evolving energy corridor due to its extensive infrastructure, strategic geographic position and supportive investment environment. The country’s existing LNG export terminals provide a significant advantage by enabling the rapid commercialization of offshore discoveries and facilitating exports to European and global markets. The Narges project also reinforces Egypt’s position as a critical energy bridge connecting Africa, the Middle East and Europe. As European nations continue seeking diversified natural gas suppliers amid geopolitical uncertainty and supply disruptions, Eastern Mediterranean gas projects have gained increasing international relevance. Chevron’s investment in the Narges field reflects broader industry confidence in the commercial viability of Mediterranean offshore exploration. The company views Egypt and the wider Eastern Mediterranean region as essential pillars within its future operational roadmap. Chevron’s drilling operations at Narges align closely with its broader strategic objective of significantly increasing production capacity throughout the Eastern Mediterranean over the next five years. During the Egypt Energy Show, Clay Neff, president of Exploration Operations at Chevron, confirmed plans to deepen its regional presence through additional offshore drilling campaigns and expanded exploration activities. According to Neff, Chevron intends to increase operational output in the region by as much as 50%, with Egypt playing a central role in achieving that target. In addition to the Narges field, CVX is also pursuing further exploration projects in the Western Mediterranean in partnership with Shell plcSHEL, highlighting its aggressive expansion strategy in offshore gas development. The decision to scale up operations reflects growing global demand for natural gas as countries transition toward cleaner-burning energy alternatives. Natural gas continues to play a critical role in international energy systems, particularly as governments seek to balance economic growth, energy security and emissions reduction goals. Chevron’s expansion strategy also underscores its confidence in Egypt’s long-term investment climate. Stable regulatory frameworks, established infrastructure and strong cooperation between international operators and Egyptian authorities have created favorable conditions for sustained offshore development. Egypt’s offshore energy sector is attracting increasing global attention as international energy companies race to secure opportunities in the Eastern Mediterranean. The successful development of large-scale projects such as Zohr previously demonstrated the immense geological potential of the region, encouraging additional exploration and investment activity. The Narges field may become another transformative asset capable of strengthening Egypt’s role as both a major producer and exporter of natural gas. Industry analysts believe continued exploration success across the Mediterranean basin could significantly enhance Egypt’s influence within international energy markets over the coming decade. The country’s advanced LNG export infrastructure remains one of its strongest competitive advantages. Unlike many emerging gas-producing nations, Egypt already possesses operational export facilities capable of connecting offshore production directly to international buyers. This infrastructure allows newly discovered reserves to move toward commercialization more rapidly than in less developed regions. At the same time, Egypt’s strategic location offers direct access to European energy markets, which remain highly focused on securing diversified and reliable gas supplies. As global competition for energy resources intensifies, Egypt’s offshore sector is becoming increasingly valuable from both economic and geopolitical perspectives. The continued development of the Narges field is expected to generate substantial economic benefits for Egypt while supporting long-term growth across the domestic energy industry. Increased offshore production can help reduce the country’s dependence on imported fuel while improving overall energy reliability for industrial and residential consumers. The project is also expected to contribute to higher government revenues through taxes, royalties and export earnings. Expanding offshore activity supports employment opportunities across multiple sectors, including engineering, logistics, maritime services, transportation and energy infrastructure development. For Chevron and its partners, the Narges field represents an opportunity to capitalize on rising international demand for natural gas while strengthening their positions within one of the world’s most promising offshore exploration regions. Continued success in Egypt’s Mediterranean waters could encourage further investment and unlock additional discoveries capable of reshaping the region’s energy future. Chevron’s latest drilling campaign at the Narges field signals a major step forward for Egypt’s offshore natural gas ambitions. With strong international partnerships, advanced export infrastructure and increasing government support for exploration activities, Egypt is positioning itself as a dominant force within the Eastern Mediterranean energy landscape. As drilling operations progress and production development accelerates, the Narges field could become a key contributor to Egypt’s domestic energy strategy and export capabilities. Chevron’s long-term commitment to expanding regional production further confirms the strategic significance of Egypt within the evolving global natural gas market. The coming years are expected to bring intensified exploration activity, additional foreign investment and expanded offshore development projects throughout the Mediterranean basin. Egypt’s ability to rapidly advance discoveries such as Narges into production may ultimately define its future role as one of the world’s most influential emerging energy hubs.
